analysis.one_liner: Ambuja Cements is India's third-largest cement maker, part of the Adani Group, producing and selling grey cement and clinker nationwide, and now set to absorb ACC and Orient Cement into one entity.
tags: Q2 PAT down on high tax base a year ago
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to September 2026) were released on 2026-10-29. Revenue was flat YoY at about ₹9,170-9,200 crore, but EBITDA fell roughly 28% as cost per tonne rose to about ₹4,410 from ₹4,155 on higher diesel, coal and petcoke costs. Reported consolidated profit fell 84-90% YoY (sources vary between ₹193 crore and ₹236 crore), but that comparison is misleading - the year-ago quarter included a one-off ₹1,697 crore income-tax provision reversal. Stripped of that, normalized profit still fell about 54% YoY to roughly ₹300 crore. Separately, the board-approved merger of ACC and Orient Cement into Ambuja is moving to the NCLT for approval.
analysis.plain_terms: The headline '90% profit crash' is mostly an illusion caused by a one-time tax credit the company booked a year ago - once you strip that out, profit still fell by about half, which is the real story. The business is selling roughly the same amount of cement as last year, at the same price, but it is costing more to make - fuel and coal got more expensive, and that extra cost ate straight into margins. Meanwhile the stock itself has been a poor investment: it is roughly half of its 2024 peak and has lost money for anyone holding it over the last one, three or five years, even as the overall market and its closest rival rose.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27: revenue ~₹9,166-9,197 crore (flat YoY), EBITDA ~₹1,240-1,271 crore (down ~28% YoY), EBITDA margin 13.5-13.8% versus 18.8-19.2% a year ago, EBITDA per tonne ₹770 versus ₹1,061. Volumes were about 16.5 million tonnes, roughly flat to slightly down YoY, while trade (retail) volumes rose 8.6% and now make up 74% of sales, with premium products at 37% of trade mix. Reported PAT fell sharply but is not comparable YoY because the year-ago quarter had a ₹1,697 crore one-off tax reversal; normalized PAT fell about 54% to roughly ₹300 crore, which is the more honest read. Management flagged diesel (+25-30%), coal/petcoke costs and geopolitical disruption (~₹228/tonne impact) as the drag, and guided to a ₹4,250/tonne cost target for FY27 and ₹4,000/tonne for FY28, with price hikes of ₹10-15 and above-industry volume growth expected in H2 FY27.
analysis.performance_read: The stock closed at ₹348.05 on 2026-10-30, down 49.5% from its July 2024 peak of ₹689.05. Over 1 year it is down 38.4% versus Nifty -10.9% and peer UltraTech -6.5%; over 3 and 5 years it remains down in absolute terms (-17% and -11.7%) while the Nifty gained over 20-28% and UltraTech gained 35-48% in the same periods. This is a genuine, sustained underperformance, not a corporate-action artifact - the only split on record is a 5:1 split in 2005, long before this period, and there has been no demerger to distort the raw price series.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates cluster around 18-21x and P/B around 1.5-1.7x, which looks cheap next to UltraTech (whose P/E is roughly double, per some sources). But the gap exists because Ambuja's return ratios are genuinely weaker - ROE around 8-10% and ROCE around 5-6% - not because the market is mispricing a comparable business. Cheap here reflects lower profitability, not a hidden bargain.
analysis.growth_read: Volumes were roughly flat to slightly down (16.5 million tonnes, about -1% YoY) and revenue was flat, so this is not a volume-growth story right now. The quarter's drama was entirely cost-side: margin compressed because fuel and coal costs rose faster than realizations, not because demand weakened or improved. The medium-term growth lever is capacity (113.5 MTPA now, targeting ~119 MTPA) and merger synergies from folding in ACC and Orient Cement, which have yet to show up in volumes.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet risk is low: the company reports a debt-free position, AAA/A1+ credit rating, net worth of about ₹71,846 crore and cash of about ₹1,770 crore (FY26-end). The real concern is business/capital-efficiency risk, not financial risk - ROE of roughly 8-10% and ROCE of roughly 5-6% are modest for a company sitting on that much net worth, suggesting the large asset and equity base (built up through past capital raises and acquisitions) isn't yet generating proportionate returns. Cash conversion of profit (operating cash flow versus PAT) was not independently verified - check on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the Adani Group, holding through entities Holderind, Harmonia and Endeavour, at 67.33% as of September 2026, unchanged quarter on quarter. These promoter entities have encumbered about 99.5% of their holding (66.94% of total equity) against a $1.375 billion credit facility - this is not a pledge on Ambuja's own shares in the sense of a default risk to the company, but it is a meaningful leverage signal at the promoter level worth watching. FIIs hold 5.63% and DIIs (mutual funds/insurers) hold 19.65%; there is no marquee individual investor on the register.
strengths: Debt-free balance sheet, AAA/A1+ rating, net worth of about ₹71,846 crore and cash of about ₹1,770 crore at FY26-end
Trade (retail) volumes up 8.6% YoY to 74% of sales mix, with premium products at 37% of trade sales (+2pp) - a shift toward higher-margin channels
Valuation discount to UltraTech on P/E, even after accounting for weaker return ratios
Capacity scaled to 113.5 MTPA after adding 4.6 MTPA this quarter, with another 5.6 MTPA ramping in H2 FY27 plus the pending ACC/Orient Cement consolidation
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell to 13.5-13.8% from 18.8-19.2% YoY as cost per tonne rose to about ₹4,410 from ₹4,155 on diesel, coal and petcoke inflation
Even after removing the one-off tax-reversal base effect, normalized profit still fell about 54% YoY to roughly ₹300 crore - the underlying weakness is real, not just an optical YoY comparison
Stock is down 49.5% from its July 2024 peak and has posted negative absolute returns over 1, 3 and 5 years while the Nifty and UltraTech rose over the same periods
Promoter entities have encumbered about 67% of total equity for a large credit facility - not a direct pledge on Ambuja shares, but a promoter-level leverage point to track
analysis.one_thing: Whether management actually hits its ₹4,250/tonne FY27 cost target and delivers the promised H2 FY27 price hikes and above-industry volume growth - if costs keep outrunning realizations, margin compression continues regardless of the ACC/Orient Cement merger synergies.
analysis.data_notes: Revenue (~₹9,166-9,197 crore) and EBITDA margin (13.5-13.8% vs ~19%) were consistent across Upstox, Kotak Neo and Business Standard. Reported consolidated PAT varied by source (₹193 crore vs ₹236 crore) - the ₹114 crore figure appears to be a standalone (not consolidated) number and was set aside. Used normalized PAT (~₹300 crore, -54% YoY) as the cleaner comparison given the disclosed ₹1,697 crore one-off tax reversal in the year-ago quarter. Valuation ratios (P/E 18-21x, ROE 8-10%, ROCE 5-6%) differed across secondary sources and were not reconciled to a single filing - treat any single-decimal figure as Not verified - check on Screener. Shareholding figures (67.33% promoter holding, 66.94% encumbrance) were corroborated across two independent trackers.
